pr_title: dts: bindings: Introduce base sensor device properties
pr_body:
Introduces an initial set of devicetree properties to be inherited by
all sensor devices, similar to how we define a base set of devicetree
properties for I2C and SPI devices. These properties will be used by the
future sensor subsystem to manage and expose sensors to a host operating
system, through HID or another protocol.

Signed-off-by: Maureen Helm <maureen.helm@intel.com>

Fixes #48148
cc: @huhebo

A key difference between this proposal and those discussed in #48148 and #45370 is that existing sensor drivers inherit base sensor properties and don't require corresponding shim nodes for the sensor subsystem. This is one less level of indirection and puts properties like vendor and model name with the physical device. Virtual sensors also inherit base sensor properties, but unlike physical sensors, they don't inherit communication bus properties from `i2c-device.yaml` or `spi-device.yaml`.

Instantiation of data structures that contain these properties takes some inspiration from network interfaces and utilizes iterable sections to allow enumeration of all sensor drivers in the system.

Further details are documented in commit messages in this PR. If this approach is accepted, I'll extend it to all the other vendors (currently I only instrumented ST and NXP sensors).

## Example 1: Physical and mocked virtual sensors
```
 $ west build -b frdm_k64f -p auto samples/sensor/sensor_shell/ -- -DSHIELD=x_nucleo_iks01a3
```
```console
uart:~$ sensor info
0xc6e8: device: 0xc2e8, vendor: STMicroelectronics, model: LPS22HH, friendly_name: 
0xc6f8: device: 0xc318, vendor: STMicroelectronics, model: STTS751, friendly_name: 
0xc708: device: 0xc300, vendor: STMicroelectronics, model: LSM6DSO, friendly_name: Base Accelerometer/Gyroscope
0xc718: device: 0xc2b8, vendor: STMicroelectronics, model: LIS2DW12, friendly_name: Lid Accelerometer
0xc728: device: 0xc270, vendor: Vendor, model: Hingle Angle, friendly_name: Hinge Angle
0xc738: device: 0xc2d0, vendor: STMicroelectronics, model: LIS2MDL, friendly_name: Base Magnetometer
0xc748: device: 0xc258, vendor: Vendor, model: Kalman Filter, friendly_name: Orientation
0xc758: device: 0xc288, vendor: NXP, model: FXOS8700, friendly_name: 
0xc768: device: 0xc2a0, vendor: STMicroelectronics, model: HTS221, friendly_name: 
```
## Example 2: Physical sensors on a different board
```
$ west build -b reel_board -p auto samples/sensor/sensor_shell/
```
```console
uart:~$ sensor info
0xbda0: device: 0xbb84, vendor: NXP, model: FXOS8700, friendly_name: 
```
Note that other sensors on the reel board don't yet appear in the console because I've only instrumented ST and NXP sensors.
pr_comments:
> I really like the sensor info command here and the general changes to DT make sense to me. Are the vendor/model properties maybe more broadly useful beyond sensors? I would think so.
> 
> I of course like that custom macro for sensors here, and easily leads to hopefully some stats and fixing the sensor get shell command to only list sensors. Might be worth tacking on here or shortly after.
> 
> The virtual sensor stuff I'm not sure makes sense in the context of this PR but I get its important to show how it would work with senss/chre.
> 
> Is it required to use the SENSOR_ device define macros to avoid breaking things? If so this is a breaking API change (I broke i2c in a way..) for external trees/drivers. Something to note.

I also very like the sensor info command, and can be leveraged in `senss` also :)

@MaureenHelm The last commit in this PR https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/49374 shows a POC implementation of how to assign vendor and model to sensors using the new properties files, and how to create a list of sensors and their properties at compile time using the multi api device model.

What do you think?

issue_context.title: Sensor Subsystem: Base sensor DTS bindings
comments: Is it important to capture device or firmware revision at the DT level, if this isn't something that can easily be determined from registers at run time, and different device revisions behave differently in a non-trivial way?

> Is it important to capture device or firmware revision at the DT level, if this isn't something that can easily be determined from registers at run time, and different device revisions behave differently in a non-trivial way?

Thinking about this, if there is value in setting revision in DT it should probably be in the specific driver binding, not the generic sensor binding since the data type may vary from one sensor to another.

> > Is it important to capture device or firmware revision at the DT level, if this isn't something that can easily be determined from registers at run time, and different device revisions behave differently in a non-trivial way?
> 
> Thinking about this, if there is value in setting revision in DT it should probably be in the specific driver binding, not the generic sensor binding since the data type may vary from one sensor to another.

I agree, I didn't want to add more to the device API because I'm already in the process of trying to get a v2 API up and running to support more use cases (https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/44098). I also think that this is pretty unique to a small subset of applications that might want to expose this information to the user (the use for the vendor/model/friendly-name fields came from the HID spec). I think that having it as a separate metadata node is reasonable in order to avoid applications that don't need this information from having to compile it in.

Can you give an example dts snippet of use here.  Vendor, model info should effectively be encoded in the compatible so those don't make sense to me.  Not sure about friendly-name either.  At least from a standard zephyr binding point of view.

Seems this topic is a discussion to #45370, especially for the [Device Tree Configuration](https://github.com/huhebo/zephyr/blob/subsys/sensorsubsys/doc/services/senss/index.rst#id41) section.

I do agree the proposal in #45370 is not perfect at current and need more improvements, and the #49294 is a good solution and discussion for this topic, especially for the `vendor`, `model`, `friendly-name`, `reporters`, `rotation-matrix` properties.  

@yperess, some explanations for your comments:  

> 2. sensor-index should not be specified by the application, it's assigned by the subsystem and should not be guaranteed to be the same across builds. Having to specify this manually makes it difficult to add/remove new entries in the middle.

Both chre and [windows](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/api/windows.devices.sensors.accelerometer.getdefault?view=winrt-22621#windows-devices-sensors-accelerometer-getdefault(windows-devices-sensors-accelerometerreadingtype)) have the `default` sensor instance concepts of a same type, such as the [chre](https://cs.android.com/android/platform/superproject/+/master:system/chre/chre_api/include/chre_api/chre/sensor.h;l=735) mentioned:  

  ```c
    For CHRE implementations that support multiple sensors of the same sensor
    type, this method can be used to get the non-default sensor(s). The default
    sensor, as defined in the chreSensorFindDefault(), will be returned if
    a sensor index of zero is specified.
  ```
  So, `sensor index` concepts is not just a internal instance id which can be generated and not consistent across builds, the `zero` index is also means the `default` sensor instance of that type, and can be get by App using `chreSensorFindDefault()`.

  I think we need make the `default` sensor instance consistent across builds, and also platform vendor need a config method to define which sensor instance is the `default` sensor.        

  Since the chre or windows only care about the `default` sensor, maybe we can just using a `default` property for the sensor instance definition in dts, but I think using a `sensor index` concepts for all sensors, and keep consistent across builds is more better.

  Or, maybe if we don't want a explicit `sensor-index` property, we can use the implicit sensor node present order in the dts as the sensor index, that's means the first present sensor instance node for a sensor type is the `default` sensor instance of this type.  

> 4. I'm not sure why minimal-interval needs to be specified here. It's a component of the physical driver and can be attained through the sensor API.

`minimal-inerval` also suitable for the virtual sensor, the consideration here is with the same sensor code implementation (virtual or physical), we can use dts to config different sensor instance with the different minimal report interval according requirements.

I think there might have been a misunderstanding with the title of this issue, my concern isn't that the sensor index exists. Just that it's specified in the device tree.

> > 4. I'm not sure why minimal-interval needs to be specified here. It's a component of the physical driver and can be attained through the sensor API.

Right, but same as my comment above, why is this specified in devicetree? I'm not saying that sensors don't need to be able to report the minimal interval to the clients, just that it doesn't belong in the devicetree.
